newsitem.title: ITALY: Centrist leader won't rule out Italy minority gvt.
newsitem.headline: Centrist leader won't rule out Italy minority gvt.

text.p: The leader of the centrist Popular Party (PPI) in Italy's coalition said on Friday that a minority government should not be ruled out if Prime Minister Romano Prodi's administration fell over strains with the hard left.
The remarks by PPI leader Franco Marini at a news conference put him at odds with the dominant force in the centre-left coalition, the ex-communist Democratic Party of the Left (PDS).
It says there would be no alternative to an early general election if Prodi's government, installed last May, has to go.

Tensions in the coalition's uneasy alliance with the hard-left party Communist Refoundation have risen this week over Refoundation's refusal to back deployment of Italian forces in Albania at the head of a planned multinational security force.
Refoundation, which is not part of the government but whose votes secure its majority in parliament's lower house, confirmed on Friday that it remained opposed to the mission.
Marini said he wanted a review of the alliance as a result of the rift to determine whether it could survive and agree a medium-term policy programme.
"If despite our efforts this indispensable clarification turns out to be impossible, it does not go without saying that the answer has to be an automatic return to the polls.

"The superior interests of the country and the primary objective of entering Europe (as part of the single currency) could determine the usefulness of a...minority government that finds the necessary consensus in parliament," Marini said.
Such a minority government would have to rely on support in parliament from the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance bloc led by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.
